title: Public corrections process + changelog convention
context: When a reader notices an error in a published explainer — a wrong figure, stale data, or misleading framing — there must be a defined, public process for reporting, triaging, fixing, and logging the correction. Without this, corrections happen ad hoc or not at all, eroding trust. The process must also specify a changelog convention so each explainer records its correction history.
objective: Define and document the public corrections process and changelog convention for open-data-explainers, and commit the process so it is linked from the project README.
acceptanceCriteria: A corrections process document specifies how a reader reports an error (e.g. a GitHub issue template or dedicated email), how it is triaged, who is responsible for fixing it, and the expected response time.
A changelog convention is defined for recording corrections on each explainer (e.g. a CORRECTIONS.md or a per-explainer changelog section with date, description, and severity).
The corrections process document is committed to the repo and linked from the project README.
resources: toolkit-002 (prerequisite — shared toolkit must exist before corrections can reference it)
output: A committed corrections process document + changelog convention (e.g. CORRECTIONS.md or a CONTRIBUTING.md update), linked from the project README.
